column1: # docs/imports.tsv -- every tracked file, under exactly one row: which import
# batch it came with and what licence applies to it. THIRD_PARTY.md is
#   glob     a path from the repository root, matched with File.fnmatch
#            (FNM_PATHNAME, FNM_EXTGLOB and FNM_DOTMATCH: `*` stays in one
#   batch    `original` (written here), or batch names declared by an
#            `@batch` line below, joined with `+` when a directory holds
#   license  MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0,
#            BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, zlib, Unicode-3.0, project
#            (written here: the project licence, Apache-2.0 WITH
#            LLVM-exception, in LICENSE), project-ported (ported from the
#            owner's earlier repositories, which stated no licence; the
#            owner put them under the project licence on 2026-11-20), joined
#            with `+` when a file carries two
#   note     anything the review needs to know
# `@batch NAME HEADING` declares a batch: HEADING is the heading of its
# section in docs/provenance.md, without the leading #s.
# tools/provenance/check-imports.rb fails when a tracked file is under no row
# or under two, a row matches no tracked file, a batch or licence is not
# declared, or a file's SPDX-License-Identifier names a licence its row does
# not (a project-ported row only counts them: a file's own SPDX line keeps
# its licence). Every import adds its rows in the same commit; so does every
# new file a row does not already cover.
# Files written here inside an imported directory are project, and so are the
# notices written here for imports. A README translated or
# rewritten here from the source's own, and an imported file rewritten here,
# stay with the batch, and the note says so.
